title: Audit stream encryption, field-mask policies, and tenant-scoped retention
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Goal: Implement governance controls across the observability pipelines so that audit and telemetry data are encrypted in transit and at rest, sensitive fields are masked at source or before landing, and retention is enforceable per-tenant. Scope includes trace spans, structured logs, and metric labels that enter the central observability platform. This ticket captures the engineering design, required infra changes, and rollout plan to provide tenant-scoped retention windows, field-mask enforcement, KMS-backed envelope encryption for audit streams, and RBAC for audit access queries. The motivation is to meet enterprise compliance requirements (GDPR/CCPA/ISO) and support customer requests for different retention and encryption controls without compromising platform observability reliability.
acceptance_criteria: Audit pipeline streams are encrypted using envelope encryption with customer or platform-managed keys (KMS)
Field-mask rules can be declared per-schema and applied at ingest or pre-landing with a configurable suppression/replace policy
Per-tenant retention policy enforced end-to-end: historical data beyond tenant TTL is deleted or archived automatically
RBAC layer restricts access to raw audit entries; access logs are generated for every read of audit data
Automated integration tests validate masking rules for 5 canonical PII types (email, ssn, phone, ip, token) and confirm no masked data is present in raw storage for masked tenants
Dashboard and alerting additions show retention enforcement lag and encryption health metrics
technical_notes: Use Kafka topics for audit stream; apply Kafka Connect transformer that performs field-mask and schema validation before write to topic partition
Implement envelope encryption in the sink connector: data encrypted with per-stream DEKs and DEKs wrapped by KMS CMKs (support both platform CMKs and customer-provided BYOK via KMS/HSM)
Retention enforcement service will run as a scheduled job per storage backend: S3 lifecycle for logs, time-based indices TTL for clickhouse/warehouse, and metadata-driven deletion for trace KV stores
Add tenant_id tag to all observational data and make it the primary shard key for retention and RBAC decisions
Introduce immutable legal-hold label for audit entries where deletion is blocked (legal-compliance use cases), with manual override flow and audit trail
Access logs for audit queries will be written to a separate encrypted topic and retained for configurable period (default 90 days) to support audits

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Masking at ingest can increase latency for high-QPS customers. Mitigation: Transformer runs in a separate thread pool with bounded concurrency and async commit; apply batching when safe.
Risk: Key management complexity when supporting BYOK. Mitigation: Start with platform-managed CMKs and pilot BYOK with one partner; document key lifecycle and rotation steps.

Risk: Incomplete deletion due to downstream copies (analytics warehouse). Mitigation: Publish deletion events to a 'deletion-hash' topic which downstream consumers must subscribe to and act on; record proof-of-deletion metadata.
Risk: RBAC misconfiguration exposing raw audit data. Mitigation: Default deny policy, integration tests for roles, and automated policy drift detection alerts.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (pilot): Enable masking and encryption for two internal tenants and two partner tenants; run retention enforcement in dry-run mode (no deletion) for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (canary): Enable deletion and BYOK support for partner tenants; collect proof-of-deletion reports and iterate
Phase 3 (general): Roll out to all dedicated tenants with UI to configure retention and key selection; provide migration scripts for archived datasets
Backout: Retention enforcement can be paused via feature-flag and a manual freeze endpoint for emergency investigations
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout via console: encryption and masking toggles per-tenant
Telemetry: create dashboards for masking-rate, encryption-errors, retention-lag, and access-log spikes
Canary tenants: select two high-throughput tenants and two low-throughput tenants to validate behavior under load
Post-rollout 30-day review with Security and Compliance teams to confirm controls meet requirements
qa_checks: Unit tests for masking transformer including nested arrays and edge-case schema variations
Integration test that ingests synthetic PII and verifies no raw PII in S3 for masked tenants
E2E throughput test to confirm pipeline latency impact < 5% for 95th percentile when masking enabled
KMS rotation test to ensure wrapped DEKs are re-wrapped and accessible after rotation
Access control test asserting that RBAC prevents tenant B from querying tenant A audit data
